project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas Fraxinus + Forestiera visual module
project_scope.note: Canonical Fraxinus species are clickable; Forestiera remains a family-reference anchor.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at the node: local Oleaceae is woody, usually opposite/subopposite, and lacks stipules. Then read leaf architecture and fruit.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Fraxinus has odd-pinnate compound leaves; Forestiera has simple leaves.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Often small; corolla may be absent in local focal genera.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Fraxinus makes a samara; Forestiera makes a one-seeded drupe.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Opposite leaves alone are not enough—fruit type is the fast local separator.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Oleaceae is easiest locally when you pair opposite branching with the fruit: ash keys versus Forestiera drupes.

comparisons.title: Oleaceae vs Rubiaceae
comparisons.rule: Rubiaceae usually has interpetiolar stipules and an inferior ovary; Oleaceae lacks stipules and has a superior ovary.

comparisons.title: Ash vs boxelder
comparisons.rule: Fraxinus makes single samaras; Acer negundo makes paired samaras.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not teach Oleaceae as 'opposite leaves + four white petals'; the local focal genera often have reduced or absent corollas.

family_confusion_polish.look_here_first: At a node check for interpetiolar stipules (absent in Oleaceae), then examine flower and mature fruit. Opposite leaves alone are not decisive: Menodora can have alternate upper leaves. Look for a superior ovary and route by leaf architecture, stamens, and fruit: single samara, drupe, or dry capsule.
family_confusion_polish.why_this_family: The local four-genus pool spans opposite compound-leaved ashes, simple-leaved shrubs with reduced flowers, cultivated privets with a corolla, and small-flowered Menodora. The shared family concept is not one habit or fruit type; inspect superior ovary, often two fertile stamens, lack of stipules, and genus-specific reproductive anatomy together.
important_exceptions: Menodora may have alternate upper leaves and a dry bilobed capsule; Oleaceae is not uniformly woody, opposite-leaved, or fleshy-fruited.
Forestiera can have inconspicuous apetalous flowers; four conspicuous petals are not required.
Male Fraxinus trees lack samaras. Leaflet number, leaf scars and lower-surface wax are supporting cues, not reliable family proof by themselves.
Ligustrum is retained as an encounter/comparison genus; family recognition does not change its native-range labels.

genus_routes.look: Usually opposite, odd-pinnate compound leaves; on fruiting plants a SINGLE samara with a wing attached to one seed body.
genus_routes.confirm: Wing-to-seed-body junction, leaflet underside, leaf scars. Compare Acer negundo paired samaras.

genus_routes.look: Opposite/subopposite SIMPLE leaves on stiff woody branchlets; very small often apetalous flowers, frequently before leaf flush.
genus_routes.confirm: Small dark one-seeded drupes; F. angustifolia narrow revolute leaves vs F. pubescens broader blades; elbow branching alone not a species split.

genus_routes.look: Opposite simple leaves; small flowers with a four-lobed fused corolla, usually in branching clusters.
genus_routes.confirm: Dark fleshy fruits and flower dissection; distinguish from apetalous Forestiera; introduced comparison context retained.

genus_routes.look: Small simple leaves, opposite below but sometimes alternate above; tubular flower with TWO stamens.
genus_routes.confirm: Paired/bilobed dry capsule, often two fruit lobes; do not force it into ash-samara or shrub-drupe routes.

confusable_family_matrix.similarity: Opposite simple leaves and sometimes fleshy fruits
confusable_family_matrix.separate: Inspect node for interpetiolar stipules and flower for generally inferior ovary in Rubiaceae versus exstipulate superior ovary in Oleaceae.

confusable_family_matrix.similarity: Opposite pinnately compound leaves like Fraxinus
confusable_family_matrix.separate: Acer has paired samaras; Fraxinus individual fruits are single samaras. Photograph fruit attachment, not merely a fallen wing.

confusable_family_matrix.similarity: Opposite compound leaves on woody plants
confusable_family_matrix.separate: Typically long, dehiscent capsules with many winged seeds; Fraxinus has single one-seeded samaras.

confusable_family_matrix.similarity: Opposite simple leaves and sometimes drupaceous fruit
confusable_family_matrix.separate: Dissect flower/ovary and mature fruit; node alone and dark berry color do not settle family.

family_confusion_polish.asset_policy: Reuse existing canonical Fraxinus and Forestiera study anchors, Calvin/Joey frames where diagnostically suitable and licensed. These are diagnostic-photo assignments, not claims that new images have been acquired.
family_confusion_polish.taxonomy_handoff: Do not alter accepted names or native-range decisions. F. angustifolia here means Forestiera angustifolia, not Fraxinus. Fraxinus greggii unresolved range state remains separate from learner admission.
